title: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 9](/bible/2-samuel/9)

## Introduction

This session covers 2 Samuel 9-12. It is a short day, but it carries a heavy weight: David's love for his people, his war against the children of Ammon and the Syrians, and then his great fall with Bathsheba and the murder of Uriah, followed by the judgment the Most High brought upon his house. Chapter 9 shows David seeking out the house of Saul so that he may show kindness for Jonathan's sake, restoring all of Saul's land to Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth and seating him at the king's table continually. This is the same love and care Israel needs to bring back: when we lose people in Israel, we take care of their family as if they were there themselves. That is why the Most High called David a man after his own heart; David loved his people so much that even though things did not go well between him and Saul, he still had enough love for Jonathan to take care of his seed.

**[2 Samuel 9:1](/bible/2-samuel/9#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/9#v1)</sup> And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?

- David asked whether there was yet any left of the house of Saul that he might show him kindness for Jonathan's sake. Remember that Saul's son Jonathan and David were always very close.
- That closeness goes back to the beef between Saul and David in the book of Samuel; Jonathan was always there for David, that was David's homeboy, they were really close.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Samuel 18:3](/bible/1-samuel/18#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/18#v3)</sup> Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.

    Jonathan and David made a covenant because he loved him as his own soul.

**[2 Samuel 9:2-5](/bible/2-samuel/9#v2)**

> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/9#v2)</sup> And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/9#v3)</sup> And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, which is lame on his feet.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/9#v4)</sup> And the king said unto him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo–debar.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/9#v5)</sup> Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lo–debar.

- A servant of the house of Saul named Ziba was brought to David. When David asked whether there was yet any of the house of Saul that he might show the kindness of God unto him, Ziba said Jonathan had yet a son who was lame on his feet, dwelling in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel in Lodebar.
- The king sent and fetched him out of Lodebar. Because of the respect and love David had for Jonathan, David was going to show kindness to Jonathan's son, even though the son could not walk.

**[2 Samuel 9:6-7](/bible/2-samuel/9#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/9#v6)</sup> Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come unto David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/9#v7)</sup> And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

- When Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan came unto David he fell on his face and did reverence. David told him, Fear not, for I will surely show thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father, and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
- To show his love for Jonathan, David gave everything that Saul owned to Jonathan's son.

**[2 Samuel 9:8-11](/bible/2-samuel/9#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/9#v8)</sup> And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am?
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/9#v9)</sup> Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him, I have given unto thy master’s son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/9#v10)</sup> Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in the fruits, that thy master’s son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master’s son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/9#v11)</sup> Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.

- Mephibosheth bowed himself and asked what David saw in such a dead dog as he was. David then called Ziba and gave unto his master's son all that pertained to Saul, and charged Ziba, his sons, and his servants to till the land and bring in the fruits, that Mephibosheth might have food, though he himself would eat at the king's table always.
- Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants. This shows the level of riches Israel had as a nation: Saul's servant had servants of his own, that is how wealthy this man was, and all of them were set to till the land and take care of the house for Mephibosheth, all out of the respect David had for Jonathan.

**[2 Samuel 9:12-13](/bible/2-samuel/9#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/9#v12)</sup> And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/9#v13)</sup> So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.

- Mephibosheth had a young son named Micha, and all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth, who dwelt in Jerusalem and did eat continually at the king's table, and was lame on both his feet.
- This is what we need to bring back into Israel: this same love, care, and admiration for the people we lose. It is unfortunate, but we do lose people in Israel, and we need to take care of their family as if they were there themselves. That is why the Most High said David is a man after his own heart; David loved his people, grounding Jonathan's family and establishing his seed in Israel.
